chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban ibn ʿUthman, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man became junub in his garment, and he did not have any garment other than it.
He عليه السلام said: He prays in it, and when he finds water, he washes it.

So this report bears two possibilities. One of them—and it is the more likely—is that some najasah from semen had reached the garment; in that case, he prays in it if he does not find another and cannot remove it, and repetition of the prayer would be upon him according to what we explained earlier.
And it is also possible that what is meant is when janabah from what is haram affected him and he perspired in it; then he prays in it, and when he finds water, he washes it.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Can a person pray in a garment affected by janabah if no other garment is available?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on praying in a garment associated with janabah when no other garment is available. The accompanying explanation presents two possible understandings: either the garment was affected by najasah from semen, or the case concerns perspiration in the garment after janabah from a haram act.
